claims.statement: The API process never generates documentation: it only creates wiki rows in the queued state, serves status/logs/download, and requeues claims whose workers stopped heartbeating; generation happens exclusively in worker processes.

The API and worker containers share no in-process channel and never call each other; they coordinate only through the shared /data volume, where SQLite holds the wiki registry and jobs/<wiki_id>/ holds workspace, logs.txt and wiki.zip.

Both roles run from a single image: the api service uses the image's uvicorn factory CMD while the worker service overrides the command with `python -m app.worker` and shares the same named volume, and worker concurrency is scaled with replicas (`--scale worker=N`) times MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS per container.

The queue hands out work atomically: claim_next opens an explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction and performs a conditional UPDATE on status='queued', so two workers on separate connections can never claim the same wiki, and the winner is moved to fetching with a fresh claim_id and incremented attempts.

Progress updates double as the claim lease and as the cancellation channel: heartbeat refreshes last_seen_at, returns ok=False when the lease was lost (reaped or completed elsewhere) and cancel=True when the API was asked to cancel, and the worker turns either signal into its cooperative cancel event.

Resumption after a worker crash is store-driven: recover_stale requeues running wikis whose last_seen_at is older than the lease, and the API runs that sweep at startup and periodically in a background task, so another worker picks the wiki up in the same workspace.

Terminal state is claim-scoped: complete() only applies when the claim_id still matches and the wiki is in a running status, so a stale worker that lost its lease cannot overwrite a result the current owner produced.

Wiki lifecycle is queued → fetching → generating → finalizing → done (or failed/cancelled); cancel is immediate while queued and cooperative while running, and retry only requeues failed or cancelled wikis by clearing the claim state so OpenWiki resumes from its own page queue.

app/services/wiki_runner.py is the only module that invokes the OpenWiki CLI: it builds the `--init|--update -p` command, hardcodes the native openwiki/ output directory, adopts a hidden artifact dir for incremental updates, decides init vs update, writes INSTRUCTIONS.md, parses .run.json and owns the CLI environment and timeout.

Keeping OpenWiki behind wiki_runner.py makes CLI upgrades a pure image rebuild: bumping the OPENWIKI_VERSION build arg and recreating the containers requires no service code change as long as the CLI still supports `openwiki --init -p`.

The pipeline that fetches, runs the CLI, packages and optionally pushes is shared verbatim by the worker containers and by the optional in-process worker enabled with RUN_LOCAL_WORKER=true, so tests and single-container development exercise the production path.

Worker runners never die on a job error: pipeline exceptions are mapped to terminal statuses — PipelineCancelled to cancelled, PushError to failed with a push_result detail, ingestion/CLI/packaging errors to failed with a truncated message — and any unexpected exception is caught and recorded as failed.

Progress reported to the API is derived from OpenWiki's own durable run state (openwiki/.run.json) as `N/M pages · phase`, falling back to counting Markdown pages already written when no plan exists yet.

JobStore owns the on-disk workspace layout — job_dir, repo_dir, logs_path and wiki_zip_path — and validates wiki ids against a fixed 32-hex pattern before touching paths or rows, which is why the pipeline and API never compose paths themselves.

The store is the queue's schema owner: a wikis table with the lifecycle, claim, progress and result columns plus a (status, created_at) index, a workers presence table, and WAL journaling with a busy timeout so API readers and worker writers do not block each other.

The HTTP layer stays thin by design: routers validate payloads, stream uploads and delegate to the store, all business logic lives in app/services/, and adding an endpoint means a new module under app/routers/ included from create_app() rather than git or CLI calls in the route.

POST /wikis rejects at the door configurations the worker could not satisfy: no response is queued when the URL scheme is unsupported, when a token is combined with a non-http(s) URL, or when push is requested without an http(s) URL and a PAT (SSH keys and git:// are refused).

The two health endpoints have deliberately different costs: GET /health reports version, data_dir, pool stats and the passive model configuration without contacting any provider, while GET /health/model sends an active minimal probe (cached for MODEL_CHECK_TTL_SECONDS) and answers 503 when the model is not configured or does not respond.

Operational limits are explicit: the queue and artifacts assume one host with a local volume (multi-host requires replacing app/core/storage.py with a Postgres backend exposing the same methods and sharing the artifact tree), the API has no authentication, and a submitted PAT is persisted in the volume database outside logs and responses so a wiki can be retried without resending it.

When OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_EXTRA_HEADERS is configured, the worker starts a loopback forwarding proxy and points the CLI's OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL at it so required gateway headers are injected, while the CLI subprocess receives that override through the worker's env_overrides.

Test coverage of the whole system runs without a model provider or network: the suite points OPENWIKI_BIN at tests/fixtures/fake_openwiki.py with run_local_worker=True to drive the real pipeline end to end, and separately unit-tests the queue contract (atomic claims, heartbeat/cancel, stale-claim requeue, worker stats, legacy job.json migration).

Provider configuration is deliberately outside the service's `Settings`: provider credentials are never declared there but stay in the process environment and are forwarded untouched to the OpenWiki subprocess, which only has `OPENWIKI_CONFIG_DIR` and `OPENWIKI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` forced; all provider knowledge (the provider table and the active probe) lives in `app/services/model_status.py`.

Besides serving status, the API also owns two storage-side filesystem duties on the shared volume: POST /wikis/upload streams the archive into jobs/<wiki_id>/upload<ext> (deleting the just-created row when the upload exceeds MAX_UPLOAD_MB), and DELETE /wikis/{id} plus the JOB_RETENTION_HOURS startup purge remove the row and its whole jobs/<wiki_id>/ directory tree.
